posts.title: Who Am I or Whatever? ( #IWSG )
posts.description: The Insecure Writer's Support Group Join us on the first Wednesday of each month in Alex J. Cavanaugh's Insecure Writer's Support Group --a forum of writers who gather to talk about writing and the writer's life. For a complete list of participants visit Alex's Blog . The co-hosts for the November 4 posting of the IWSG are Kalpana, Kim Lajevardi, Rebecca Douglass, Jennifer Lane, and Cathrina Constantine . November 4 question - As a writer, do you have favorite themes that you like to explore in your stories? If so, what are they? My favorite theme is one that goes back to the beginnings of storytelling: The Journey. After all a journey can be a metaphor for life or anything that involves a beginning and an end. Kind of like a story. A story is a journey of sorts that reflects something in life or what we imagine life to be. The co-hosts for the October 7 posting of the IWSG are Ronel Janse van Vuuren, Liza at Middle Passages, JH Moncrieff, and Jemima Pett . October 7 question - Many people are calling for writers who use AI to disclose it. Most who employ ghostwriters do not admit it - do you think authors who use ghostwriters should have to disclose that, too? (Thanks Melissa Maygrove for the question!) Great question for the times. It's a question of ethics I would say, but when you toss ghostwriters into the mix then that does put to question any endeavor in which someone claims to do something that they have not done. posts.title: Am I the Star of My Own Movie? ( #IWSG )
posts.description: The Insecure Writer's Support Group Join us on the first Wednesday of each month in Alex J. Cavanaugh's Insecure Writer's Support Group --a forum of writers who gather to talk about writing and the writer's life. For a complete list of participants visit Alex's Blog . The co-hosts for the September 2 posting of the IWSG are Kate Larkinsdale, SE White, JS Pailly, Olga Godim, and Natalie Aguirre . September 2 question - Do you have a favorite character archetype you tend to gravitate toward in your writing? If I were to come up with my favorite character type I'd have to say it is myself. My stories usually have been extensions of who I am or fantasize myself to be at any particular time. My stories are typically my stories. They read like an autobiography that might be deciphered if one knew the code. Maybe eventually I'll write more so that I'll have to go beyond myself and into the lives of others. Or maybe I'll just write memoir. Just so I write something. Anything.
